entries.answer:
[ERROR LIST]
- Line 42: `appendJsonString` writes non-ASCII bytes directly rather than validating UTF-8; invalid byte sequences in input are emitted into a JSON string, producing invalid JSON.
- Line 71: `appendJsonValue` writes `.number_string` values verbatim without validating JSON-number syntax; a malformed `number_string` value would produce invalid JSON.
- Line 164: `sendJsonRequest` converts every `client.fetch` failure into `error.HttpRequestFailed`, including allocator failures and `error.HttpResponseTooLarge`; this makes the declared `HttpResponseTooLarge` error unreachable and loses the actual failure cause.
- Line 219: `runExaSearch` accepts any nonempty `search_type`, although the advertised tool schema permits only `auto`, `instant`, or `fast`; invalid values are sent to Exa instead of being rejected locally.
- Line 219: `runExaSearch` does not enforce Exa’s valid `category` values; arbitrary nonempty category strings are forwarded to the API.
- Line 219: `runExaSearch` validates `start_published_date` and `end_published_date` only as arbitrary nonempty strings; malformed dates and an end date preceding the start date are not rejected.
- Line 292: `runExaGetContents` has no upper bound on `urls_array.items.len`; a model response can request an unbounded number of URLs in one API call.
- Line 365: `runExaGetContents` permits `subpage_targets` when `subpages` is zero, producing an inconsistent request whose targets cannot be used.
- Line 411: `runExaDeepSearch` accepts any nonempty `search_type`, although the advertised tool schema permits only `deep-lite`, `deep`, or `deep-reasoning`; invalid values are forwarded to Exa.
- Line 460: `runExaWebsets` accepts any nonempty `enrichment_format`; formats outside `text`, `date`, `number`, `options`, `email`, `phone`, and `url` are forwarded to Exa.
- Line 477: `runExaWebsets` sends an `enrichments` object whenever `enrichment_description` is non-null, but does not require a description for non-`options` formats. It therefore accepts an empty/omitted enrichment description paired with a nonempty format, despite the intended enrichment contract.
- Line 541: `runExaWebsetItems` accepts whitespace-only `cursor` strings as an empty cursor rather than rejecting them or preserving the provided value; this silently changes the requested pagination state.
- Line 629: `appendStoredMessage` ignores the `.system` union payload and always serializes the hard-coded system message. Any future or caller-supplied system-message content is discarded.
- Line 736: `runAgent` stores `message_value` from `parsed_response` in `messages`, then appends `parsed_response` to `parsed_message_storage` only after `messages.append` succeeds. If `messages.append` fails, `parsed_response` is neither deinitialized nor retained, leaking its parse allocation.
- Line 740: If `tool_calls` exists but is not an array, `runAgent` returns `error.InvalidResponse` after storing `parsed_response`; cleanup is deferred correctly, but the already-appended assistant message is invalid and remains in `messages` until function teardown. This is not externally observable but wastes memory for the rest of unwinding.
- Line 764: When the tool-call limit would be exceeded, `runAgent` returns the literal text `"[A maximális tool-hívási korlát elérve]"` as a successful agent response instead of returning `error.ToolCallLimitReached`. The declared error is never used.
- Line 805: When the iteration limit is reached, `runAgent` returns the literal text `"[A maximális agent-iteráció elérve]"` as a successful agent response instead of returning `error.AgentIterationLimitReached`. The declared error is never used.
- Line 815: `main` catches every error from `readEnvironmentValue` and reports that the relevant environment variable is unset. Allocation failures and other environment-access failures are therefore falsely reported as missing API keys.
[END OF LIST]

FILE CLOSED. ALL ERRORS LISTED.
